80:1: The Almighty means by His saying: Abasa 80:He pulled his face back in dislike, and turned away means: and turned away, that the blind man came to him means: because the blind man came to him. It has been mentioned from some of the reciters that he lengthened the alif and extended it from that he came to him and said: that he came to him, and it is as if the meaning of the speech was for him: Did the blind man come to him? He frowned and turned away? Just as the one who recited that he was a man of wealth and children (al-Qalam 68:14) lengthened the alif from that and shortened it. He mentioned that the blind man mentioned by God in this verse is Ibn Umm Maktum, because of whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reprimanded. Mentioning the report reported about that: Sa`id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn `Urwah, from what `Urwah had presented to him, on the authority of `Aishah, who said: He frowned and turned away was revealed concerning Ibn Umm Maktun. She said: He came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and kept saying: Guide me! She said: “And there were some of the leading figures of the polytheists with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him).” She said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept turning away from him and turning to the other, saying: ‘Do you see any harm in what I say?’ He said: ‘No.’ So it was concerning this that ‘He frowned and turned away’ was revealed.” Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, He frowned and turned away * Because the blind man came to him, he said: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was conversing with Utbah bin Rabi’ah, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, and Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, and he was often standing up to them, and he was eager for them to believe, a blind man called Abdullah bin Umm Maktum came to him, walking while he was conversing with them. Abdullah began to recite to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a verse from the Qur’an, and said: O Messenger of God, teach me from what God has taught you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him, frowned in his face, and turned away, disliking his words, and turned to the others. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished and was about to go back to his family, God took some of his sight, then he shook his head, then God revealed, He frowned and turned away * Because the blind man came to him * And what do you know that perhaps he might be purified * Or be reminded and the reminder would benefit him? So when it was revealed concerning him The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, honored him and spoke to him, saying: What is your need? Do you want anything? And when he left him, he would say to him: Do you need anything? That is because God revealed: “But he who is self-sufficient, you are his caretaker. And it is not for you that he should not be purified.” Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, who said: He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him. This verse was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, If a blind man came to him, he said: A man from Banu Fihr, called Ibn Umm Maktum. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, He frowned and turned away * Because the blind man came to him: Abdullah bin Zaida, who was the son of Umm Maktum, came to him to recite it, while he was conversing with Umayya bin Khalaf, a man from the elite of Quraysh, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him, so God revealed about him what you hear: He frowned and turned away * Because the blind man came to him until His saying: So you are distracted from him (It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed him as his deputy twice after that in Medina during two battles that he led in prayer with its people. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that he saw him on the day of Al-Qadisiyyah with a black banner and wearing his armor. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Ibn Umm Maktum came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was speaking to Abi bin Khalaf, so he turned away from him. Then God revealed to him, He frowned and turned away. After that, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would honor him. Anas said: I saw him on the day of al-Qadisiyyah wearing a suit of armor and with him a black banner. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, He frowned and turned away, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, confronted a wealthy polytheist from among the Quraysh, hoping that he would believe. Then a blind man from among the Ansar, whose name was Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, came and began to question the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked him and turned away from him, and turned to the rich man. Then God admonished His Prophet, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, honored him and appointed him as his successor over Medina twice, during two battles that he participated in. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, and I asked him about the statement of God, the Exalted: He frowned and turned away * Because the blind man came to him. He said: “Ibn Umm Maktum came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his guide could see, but he could not see. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was signaling to his guide to stop, and Ibn Umm Maktum was pushing him away, but he could not see. He said: Until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, frowned, and God rebuked him for that, and said: “He frowned and turned away * Because the blind man came to him. And what do you know that he might be purified?”... until His statement: But you are distracted from it. Ibn Zayd said: It was said: If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had concealed anything from the revelation, he would have concealed this from himself. He said: And he used to approach this noble man in his ignorance, hoping that he would become Muslim, and he was distracted from this.”
80:2: God Almighty said: If a blind man came to him.
80:3: And His statement: And what do you know, perhaps he will be purified? God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And what do you know, O Muhammad, perhaps this blind man in whose face you frowned will be purified? He says: He will be purified from his sins. Ibn Zayd used to say about this: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, Perhaps he will be purified, he means he will become Muslim.
80:4: And his saying: Or he remembers and the reminder benefits him means: Or he remembers and the reminder benefits him: meaning he considers and the consideration and admonition benefit him. The reading is in the nominative case and it benefits him in apposition to his saying he remembers. It has been narrated from Asim that it is in the accusative case and the nominative case, and the accusative case is based on making it an answer with the letter fa for perhaps, as the poet said: The vicissitudes of time and its states guide us to the right path So the soul rests from its sighs and the crop is soaked from its crops And soak It is narrated in the nominative and accusative cases.
80:5: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: As for he who is satisfied with his wealth, you expose yourself to him, hoping that he will become Muslim. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: But as for him who is self-sufficient, you are his caretaker. He said: It was revealed about Al-Abbas. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, But as for he who is self-sufficient, he said: Utbah bin Rabi’ah and Shaybah bin Rabi’ah.
80:6: God Almighty says: Then you will be devoted to it.
80:7: God Almighty says: And what is it to you if he does not purify himself? He says: What is it to you if he does not purify himself from his disbelief and become Muslim?
80:8: God Almighty says: But as for he who comes to you striving, * and he fears God. He says: But as for this blind man who comes to you striving, and he fears God and is pious to Him.
80:9: God Almighty says: And he fears.
80:10: God Almighty says: But you are distracted from it. He says: So you turn away from it, and are preoccupied with something else and are negligent.
80:11: God Almighty says: No! The matter is not as you do, O Muhammad, that you frown at someone who comes to you running and he fears, and that you confront someone who is self-sufficient. It is a reminder. He says: This sermon and this surah are a reminder. He says: A sermon and a lesson.
80:12: God Almighty says: So whoever wills, let him remember it. He says: So whoever among God’s servants wills, let him remember it. He says: Let him remember God’s revelation and His revelation. The ha in His statement it is is for the surah, and in His statement he mentioned it is for the revelation and the revelation.
80:13: God Almighty says: In scrolls meaning that it is a reminder. In honored scrolls, raised and purified meaning in the Preserved Tablet, which is raised and purified by God.
80:14: God Almighty says: raised and purified.
80:15: And his saying: In the hands of scribes means: The honored scrolls are in the hands of scribes, the plural of scribe. The interpreters differed about who they were. Some of them said: They are scribes. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, in the hands of scribes, he said: scribes. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, in the hands of scribes, he said: the scribes. Others said: They are the readers. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, “So whoever wills, let him remember it. * In honored pages * Exalted and purified * In the hands of scribes.” He said: They are the reciters. Others said: They are the angels. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told us: My uncle told us: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: In the hands of scribes * Noble and pious meaning the angels. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, In the hands of scribes, noble and righteous, he said: The scribes are those who count the deeds. The most correct of the sayings is the one that says: They are the angels who travel between God and His Messenger with revelation. The ambassador of the people is the one who seeks to reconcile them. It is said: I traveled between the people, meaning I reconciled them. From this is the saying of the poet: I do not leave the embassy among my people, nor do I walk deceitfully when I walk. If the interpretation is directed to what we said: it is possible to interpret what was said by those who say they are the scribes, and what was said by those who say they are the readers, because the angels are the ones who read the books and communicate between God and His messengers.
80:16: And his saying: Noble and pious people. And pious people is the plural of pious, just as infidels is the plural of infidel, and magicians is the plural of magician. However, what is known from the speech of the Arabs is that when they pronounce a singular form, they say: a pious man, and a pious woman. And when they make it plural, they return it to the plural of fa`il, just as they said a secret man, then they said in its plural: a people of secrets. And the standard for its singular form is that it be sari. And it has been reported by hearing from some of the Arabs: a people of good and pious people. And the singular of good is good, and pious people is pious.
80:17: And His saying: How ungrateful a man is! God Almighty says: Cursed is the ungrateful man, how ungrateful he is! Mujahid said something similar to what we said about that. Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Whenever the Qur’an says killing a human being or something done to a human being, it refers to the unbeliever. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: How ungrateful a person is to be killed. I was informed that he means the unbeliever. In his saying: I disbelieve in him, there are two aspects: One of them is astonishment at his disbelief, despite God’s kindness to him and His favors to him. The other is: What is it that I disbelieve in, meaning what thing do I disbelieve in?
80:18: God Almighty says: He mentioned: From what did the disbelieving human being create his Lord that he would be arrogant and haughty about obeying his Lord and acknowledging His Oneness!
80:19: Then He, the Most High, explained from whom He created him, saying: From a sperm-drop He created him and proportioned him in various states: sometimes a sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, until his states came to pass while he was in his mother’s womb.
80:20: God Almighty says: Then He made the way easy for him. He says: Then He made the way easy for him, meaning the road. The interpreters differed about the path that He made easy for her. Some of them said: It is his exit from his mother’s womb. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then the path is made easy for him, meaning by that his exit from his mother’s womb is made easy for him. Ibn Hamid told me: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh: Then the path is made easy for him. He said: The path of kinship. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Then the path is made easy for him. He said: His exit from his mother’s womb. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Then the path is made easy for him. He said: His exit from his mother’s womb. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then He made the way easy for him. He said: He brought him out from his mother’s womb. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: the path of truth and falsehood. We made it clear to him and informed him, and made it easy for him to act upon it. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us, he said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, Then He made the way easy for him. He said: It is like His saying, Indeed, We guided him to the way, be he grateful or ungrateful. (al-Insan 76:3) Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then He made the way easy for him, he said: It is similar to, Indeed, We have guided him to the way (al-Insan 76:3). Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The path of misery and happiness, and it is like His saying: Indeed, We guided him to the way (al-Insan 76:3). Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Al-Hasan said, regarding His statement, Then He made the way easy for him, he said: The way of good. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then He made the way easy for him, he said: He guided him to Islam, which He made easy for him, and informed him of it, and the way is the way of Islam. The first of the two interpretations of this, in my opinion, is the correct one, which says: Then the path, which is the exit from his mother’s womb, is easy for him. We said that this is the more correct of the two interpretations, because it is more similar to the apparent meaning of the verse. This is because the report from God before and after it is about His description of His creation, His management of His body, and His disposition of it in various conditions. So it is better for the middle of that to be similar to what came before and after it.
80:21: And his saying: Then He caused him to die and buried him, meaning: Then He took his soul, and caused him to die after that. By his saying He caused him to die, he means: He made him have a grave. The graver is the one who buries the dead with his own hand, as Al-A’sha said: If you lean a dead person on your throat, he will live and not be transferred to the grave. The grave: is God, who ordered his servants to bury him after his death, so he made him have a grave. The Arabs say, as he mentioned to me: I cut off the camel’s tail, may God cut it off. I bit the bull’s horn, may God make it bitten. I expelled so-and-so from me, may God expel him, I made him an outcast.
80:22: And his saying: Then if God wills, He will resurrect him. He says: Then if God wills, He will resurrect him after his death and bring him back to life. It is said: God resurrected the dead, meaning: He brought him back to life. And resurrecting the dead means that he brought himself back to life. From this is the saying of the poet: Until people say from what they saw, Oh, how strange is the dead man who spreads the report.
80:23: And His statement: No, he has not yet fulfilled what he was commanded to do. God Almighty says: No, the matter is not as this disbelieving man says, that he has fulfilled God’s right over him, in himself and his wealth, but he has not yet fulfilled what his Lord commanded him to do, he has not fulfilled the obligations that his Lord imposed upon him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, when he has not fulfilled what he was commanded to do, he said: No one ever fulfills what was required of him. Al-Harith said: as it was required of him.
80:24: God Almighty says: Let this unbelieving man, who denies the Oneness of God, look at his food and how he manages it. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: So let a person look at his food and his drink. He said: at his food and drink. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, So let man look at his food: is a sign for them. The reciters differed in reading ana sabbana al-ma’ sababan I poured the water in abundance. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it with a kasra on the alif of ina as a new sentence. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with a fatha on the alif, meaning: So let the person look at I, so they put I in the position of a genitive with the intention of repeating the genitive. It may be permissible for it to be a genitive if the intention is that his food is poured out, I poured the water in abundance. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.
80:25: And His saying: We poured down water abundantly means: We sent down rain from the sky abundantly, and poured it down upon them abundantly.
80:26: God Almighty says: Then We split the earth open. He says: Then We split the earth open and made it sprouting plants.
80:27: God Almighty says: Then We caused to grow therein grain: meaning the grain of the crop, which is everything that the earth produces of grains, such as wheat, barley, and other things.
80:28: God Almighty says: And grapes meaning: And vineyards. And qadhab meaning by qadhab: fresh dates, and the people of Mecca call qat qadhab. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, and reeds, meaning: alfalfa. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And reeds. He said: And reeds are the willows. Abu Jaafar, may God have mercy on him, said: Alfalfa is the fresh date. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, and fresh dates, meaning fresh dates. Bishr told us, he said: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, he said: Yunus told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, he omitted his statement, and fodder, he said: Fodder is the fodder.
80:29: And his saying: And olives which are the olives from which oil is made, and palm trees.
80:30: God Almighty said: And thick gardens. We have already explained that a garden is a fenced orchard, and His saying thick means: thick. And by His saying thick He means trees in thick orchards. Al-Ghab is the plural of Aghlab, which is a thick-necked man, and from this is the saying of Al-Farazdaq: He howled and aroused the most of the wrath. Woe to Ibn al-Maragha for what he aroused. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about it, with differences in their explanation of it. Some of them said: It is what is intertwined and gathered from the tree. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Asim bin Kulayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And gardens of dense trees, he said: Gardens are what are intertwined and gathered together. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and gardens of abundance, he said: good. Others said: Gardens: all tree growth. Who said that? Abu Hisham told us, he said: Ibn Fadil told us, he said: Asim told us, on the authority of his father: Gardens: all tree growth. Muhammad bin Sinan Al-Qazzaz told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Shabib, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And gardens of abundant shade. He said: The trees are for shade in Paradise. Others said: Rather, al-Ghalb means: the tall ones. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And gardens of Ghaleb, meaning: tall. Others said: Are the palm trees generous? Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And gardens of abundant rain, and abundant rain means the noble palm trees. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And gardens of abundant trees, he said: The noble palm trees. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And gardens of Ghalaban,: The great trunks of palm trees. He said: And the Ghalab among men: the great necks. It is said: He is the one with the greatest neck: its greatness. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, Ghalba’s gardens, he said: The bones of the middle.
80:31: God Almighty says: Fruit is what people eat from the fruits of trees, and father is what animals eat from grass and plants. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Waki` told us, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan, And fruit, he said: What the son of Adam eats. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And fruits, he said: What people eat. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And fruit. He said: As for the fruit, it is for you. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, and fruit, he said: The fruit is for us. Humayd ibn Mas`adah narrated: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated: Humayd narrated: Anas ibn Malik said: Umar recited, He frowned and turned away, until he came to this verse, And fruits and herbage. He said: We know what fruit is, but what is herb? Then I think al-Tabari was unsure. He said: This is an exaggeration. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, recited, He frowned and turned away, and when he came to this verse, And fruits and herbage, he said: We know what fruit is, but what is herb? He said: By your life, O Ibn al-Khattab, this is indeed an exaggeration. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Musa bin Anas, on the authority of Anas, who said: `Umar recited and fruits and father while he had a stick in his hand. He said: What is father? Then he said: What we have learned is sufficient for us, and he threw the stick from his hand. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Khalid Ibn Ja`far, on the authority of Abu Iyas Mu`awiyah Ibn Qurrah, on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him, who said: This is the effort. He said: Qatada told me, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of Umar, a hadith similar to this entire hadith. Abu Kurayb, Abu al-Sa’ib, and Ya’qub told us: Ibn Idris told us: I heard Asim ibn Kulayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He counted seven, made his sustenance in seven, and made it from seven, and said at the end of that: The father is what the earth produces, of which people do not eat. Abu Hisham told us, he said: Ibn Fadil told us, he said: Asim told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The father is the plant of the earth that animals eat but people do not eat. Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us: Abd al-Malik told us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas counted and said: The father is what the earth produces for livestock. This is the wording of Abu Kurayb’s hadith. Abu al-Sa’ib said in his hadith: He said: The earth produces what people eat and livestock eat. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The father is all grass and pasture. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, who said: The father is the plant. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, the same. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash or someone else, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The father is the pasture. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan. Mujahid said: And Aba means pasture. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan, and Aba, he said: The father is what the livestock eat. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, and father, he said: Father: what the livestock eat. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: As for the father: your livestock are blessings from God that are evident. Ibn Bishr told us, he said: Abd al-Wahid told us, he said: Yunus told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement, and father, he said: Father is the grass. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan and Qatada, regarding his statement, and father, they said: It is what animals eat. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement, and Abu, meaning: the pasture. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And father, he said: The father is for our livestock. He said: And the father is what they graze. And he recited, Provision for you and for your livestock (Abasa 80:32). He said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yunus and Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, that Anas ibn Malik told him that he heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: God said, And grass, and olives, and palm trees, and gardens dense with trees, and fruits, and fodder. We have explained all of this, so what is fodder? Then he struck his hand, then said: By your life, this is an exaggeration, and follow what is made clear to you in this Book. Umar said: And whatever is made clear, then stick to it, and whatever is not, then leave it. Others said: Father: the moist fruit. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying and Abu means: fresh fruits.
80:32: And His statement: For your enjoyment means: We caused these things that the children of Adam eat to grow as enjoyment for you, O people, and as a benefit for you, and which the livestock eat for your livestock. The origin of livestock is camels, and then it is used for every grazing animal. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, Provision for you and your livestock, he said: Provision for you is fruit, and for your livestock is grass.
80:33: And his saying: And when the Deafening Blast comes, he mentioned that it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, and I think it was taken from their saying: So-and-so cried out to the voice of so-and-so, if he listened to him, except that it is said from this: he is listening to him, and perhaps the voice is the one who cried out, so if that is the case, then it should have been said that it was for the blowing of the trumpet. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then when the Deafening Blast comes, he said: This is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, which God has made great and warned His servants about.
80:34: And his saying: On the Day when a man will flee from his brother, meaning: So when the deafening blast comes, on this day when a man will flee from his brother, and by his saying flee from his brother he means fleeing from his brother.
80:36: And his companion meaning his wife who was his wife in this world and his children to avoid their demanding from him the consequences and injustices between him and them. Some of them said: The meaning of his saying: A man flees from his brother is: He flees from his brother so that he does not see him and what befalls him.
80:37: God Almighty says: For every one of them meaning the man, his brother, his mother, his father, and all those mentioned in this verse on that Day meaning the Day of Resurrection when the deafening blast comes on the Day of Resurrection will have an affair that will suffice him meaning: an affair that will suffice him and distract him from the affair of others. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Every man among them, that Day, will have enough to make him indifferent to people, means that every person will have something to occupy him from the people. Abu Umara Al-Marwazi Al-Hussein bin Harith narrated to us: Al-Fadl bin Musa narrated to us, on the authority of Aaidh bin Shuraih, on the authority of Anas, who said: “Aisha asked the Messenger of God, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, I ask you about a hadith that you yourself informed me of! He said: If I have knowledge of it, she said: O Prophet of God, how will the men be gathered? He said: Barefoot and naked. Then she waited for a while and said: O Prophet of God, how will the poor be gathered? He said: Likewise, barefoot and naked. She said: Woe to the Day of Resurrection! He said: And about that you ask me? A verse was revealed to me: It does not matter whether you have clothing or not. She said: Which verse is that, O Prophet of God? He said: ‘Every man among them that Day will have enough to make him independent of others.’” Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, For every man of them, that Day, will be a matter that will make him indifferent to his companion, he said: A matter that will distract him from his companion.
80:38: And His statement: On that Day, some faces will be radiant. God Almighty says: Some faces on that Day will be radiant and shining, and they are the faces of the believers with whom God is pleased. It is said: So-and-so’s face is radiant: if it is handsome, and from this comes the word the morning is radiant: if it shines, and everything that is radiant is radiant. As for travel without an alif, it is only said of a woman if she removes her veil or burqa from her face. It is said: A woman has unveiled her face, if she does that, so she is safir. From this comes the saying of Tawbah ibn al-Humayr: Whenever I visited Laila, I would cover myself with a veil, because her unveiling had made me suspicious the next morning. What he means by his saying her unveiling is her removing her veil from her face.
80:39: God Almighty says: Laughing meaning: Laughing with joy at what God has given her of bliss and honor. Rejoicing at what she hopes for of increase. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of his saying unveiled, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: Musafira means bright. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, laughing and rejoicing, he said: These are the people of Paradise.
80:40: And His statement: And faces that Day will be covered with dust. God Almighty says: And faces, which are the faces of the disbelievers that Day, will be covered with dust. He mentioned that the animals that God will turn into dust on that Day after judgment has been passed between them, will turn that dust into dust in the faces of the disbelievers.
80:41: God Almighty says: A darkness will cover them. He says: A darkness will cover those faces, which is dust. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, It will be covered by a state of humiliation, meaning: It will be covered by humiliation. Yusun told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, A darkness will overwhelm it, he said: These are the faces of the people of Hellfire. He said: And darkness comes from dust. He said: They are one and the same. He said: As for in this world, darkness is that which rises and reaches the sky, and the wind lifts it. The Arabs call it darkness, and that which is lower on the earth is dust.
80:42: And His statement: Those are the disbelieving, wicked ones. God Almighty says: These are the ones whose description on the Day of Resurrection is the disbelievers in God. They were wicked in their religion in this world, not caring about the sins they committed against God and the things they committed that He prohibited. So God punished them for their evil deeds, as He informed His servants of.
